mechanical.notes: 15 meshes / 4720 tris. 6/6 suites (trace, struct, framing, light, boot, float). Console clean across 4 states. SIX defects caught+fixed. The headline: a hierarchy that NAMED a mechanism it did not implement — pan_yoke was created but setTilt still applied pan AND tilt to the cradle, so the arms stayed put while the module rotated 35deg off them and the trunnions left their bearings entirely; caught by the contact graph (trunnions touching only the barrel). Fixed: pan on the yoke, tilt on the cradle, verified across pan 0/35/90 x tilt 0/22/45. THE FLOAT GUARD took three attempts and the lesson generalises: AABB overlap gives a FALSE NEGATIVE on concave shapes (a cone/tube's box contains its own empty interior, so a suspended module read 'in contact' with the shroud around it); vertex-to-vertex distance is BLIND to interpenetration (a pivot embedded 0.6 mm has no vertex near the ring's, so the strongest joint read 'floating' — and INCREASING the embed made it worse, the tell that a fix in the right direction moving the metric the wrong way means the metric measures the wrong thing). What works: point-to-SURFACE distance <= tol OR ray-parity containment restricted to meshes tagged closed-solid at construction (parity on the OPEN shroud would call the suspended module 'inside'), with ADAPTIVE sampling stride = max(1, count/96) (a fixed stride missed a 24-segment trunnion in the arm it mounts in). Other fixes: dome-edge gasket join, base/trim coincident-but-same-material seating, the containment list that had stopped covering the 4 new interior bearing pieces, and a spec/code name drift (lens_module vs lens_cradle) reconciled CODE->spec with `animation` narrowed tilt-pan -> tilt. Framing 43/43 unchanged; lighting 1.715/0.094 unchanged, metalness untouched; boot clean; 9 materials instantiated; all hierarchy names traceable.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. The structural pass turned a floating optical assembly into a real supported, articulated mechanism (pan_yoke + trunnions), and the depth of the guard work is the standout: it caught a hierarchy that named a mechanism it did not implement (worse than no hierarchy, because the names invite assuming the behaviour), and it hardened float detection through three wrong definitions to a right one — the generalisable lesson being that AABB is a false-negative on concave solids and vertex-distance is blind to interpenetration, so contact needs point-to-surface + closed-solid-tagged parity + adaptive stride. All criticals read, the mechanism articulates correctly across poses, integrity holds. Cleared to the materials pass.
